newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's CDC raises Q3 and Q4 GDP estimates.
newsitem.headline: France's CDC raises Q3 and Q4 GDP estimates.

text.p: French state bank Caisse des Depots et Consignations (CDC) on Monday revised higher its estimates for French economic growth rates in the third and fourth quarters of 1996.
It raised its estimate for third quarter gross domestic product to 0.7 percent from 0.4 percent previously and upped its estimate for fourth quarter GDP to 0.5 percent from 0.3 percent.
Its seasonally adjusted figures are based on a leading indicator composed of data published up to September 30.

CDC said in a statment the upward revisions "can be explained essentially by the rebound in household consumption (up 3.0 percent in August) which was in fact driven by surging car sales (up 18.1 percent in the month)."

"At the same time, the favourable progression of industrial output in Germany and in the United States is providing support to French growth," the statement said. "The rally on the major world stock markets coupled with dropping yields is likely to buoy growth."

CDC said, however, it was important to note that the favourable developments in consumption "offset the impact of other negative components, such as the deterioration witnessed in production and employment."
The state-owned bank also said household consumption would probably decline in October because of the end to government car buying incentives.
It said this "implies that the forecast for the fourth quarter would be scaled back" when future consumption figures were incorporated into its leading indicator.
CDC said the estimates were a synthetic index, not a forecast.
